Everything within an hour of the office

The pick

Roswell is first

It has the best downtown on the list, river and creek trails next to it, the shortest commute, low crime, and condos from $285,000 to $335,000 near Canton Street. Duluth is second on price and safety. Marietta is third: at this budget its main option is a 55+ community, and Cobb County drops school taxes at age 62.

  • Office in Sandy Springs, 3 days a week
  • Up to about an hour each way, shorter preferred
  • Small-town feel with a walkable downtown
  • Nature close by
  • 2 to 3 bedrooms, 2 to 3 baths
  • Single-level or few stairs
  • Detached, condo, townhome, or 55+ all acceptable
  • At or under $350,000, with roughly $100,000 in home equity
  • Good hospital access
  • Low crime
  • MARTA is a bonus

Commute times are my rush-hour estimates, not measured drives. Crime is per 100,000 residents from 2024 FBI data, except Tucker, which is a third-party 2026 estimate.

Safety in context

Violent crime is where the towns differ most. Woodstock, Decatur, Roswell and Duluth all sit close to Lee's Summit. Tucker is the only one above the national average.

The towns, in ranked order

Ranked for a $350,000 cap. Woodstock and Kennesaw are kept at the bottom because they fit everything except price. Each day-in-the-life sketch assumes a 9:00 start and uses my commute estimates. It is an illustration built from what each town has, not a schedule anyone reported.

A cheaper fallback: a Sandy Springs condo

Three-bedroom condos in Sandy Springs ran about $240,000 to $295,000 when this search looked at them. There is no small-town feel, but the commute is about 10 minutes and Roswell's Canton Street is about 15 minutes north. Drive times are my estimates.

Money

What the budget supports

Principal and interest at 6.5% over 30 years, assuming about $75,000 down after selling costs. Taxes and insurance are extra. The HOA column uses a $400 placeholder. Ask for the real dues on each listing.

PriceLoanMonthly P&IWith $400 HOA
$300,000$225,000about $1,420about $1,820
$325,000$250,000about $1,580about $1,980
$350,000$275,000about $1,740about $2,140
  • $70,000 is 20% down on $350,000, the point where mortgage insurance drops off.
  • Each extra $25,000 of price adds about $160 a month.
  • A $300,000 condo with $400 in dues costs about the same each month as a $365,000 house with none. Dues usually cover exterior upkeep, so it isn't all extra.
  • A comparable home runs roughly $50,000 to $100,000 more than in Springfield or Northwest Arkansas. Useful to know when salary and relocation help come up.

School tax exemption by county

School taxes are usually more than half of a Georgia property tax bill. The age they go away depends on the county.

CountyTowns hereRule
CobbMarietta, KennesawFull exemption at 62, no income limit
CherokeeWoodstockFull exemption at 62, with a cap on home value
GwinnettDuluth, Norcross, LilburnFull exemption at 65
FultonRoswellSeveral exemptions from 62, some income-tested. Verify
DeKalbTucker, DecaturFrom 62, income-tested. City of Decatur has its own rules. Verify

I'm not a tax advisor. Sources disagree on Fulton and DeKalb, so confirm with each county tax office before relying on these.

Housing types and what to ask

The four options

  • Detached ranch. Most privacy and yard. Near a walkable downtown, usually over budget. Under $350,000 in Duluth, Lilburn and Tucker, and now and then in Norcross.
  • Ranch or ground-floor condo. Step-free and close to downtown. The best fit in Roswell and Decatur at this budget.
  • 55+ community. Single-level, exterior upkeep handled, neighbors your age. At least one resident must be 55 or older. Common in Cobb, Cherokee and Duluth. Under $350,000, the Marietta community from the $300,000s is the main one in reach.
  • Townhome. Look for a main-level primary bedroom or an elevator. Many near the downtowns are three stories.

Before making an offer on a condo, townhome or 55+ home

  • Monthly dues and what they cover, especially roof and exterior.
  • The reserve study and any special assessments planned.
  • Fee simple or condo ownership.
  • Rental cap and owner-occupancy rate, which affect financing and resale.
  • Steps from parking to the front door, and inside to the primary bedroom.
  • Actual walking distance to downtown. Listings say near when they mean a mile or more.

Looked at and ruled out

PlaceWhy it dropped
Sandy Springs, Dunwoody, Brookhaven, BuckheadClosest to the office, but suburban or urban in feel, with no small-town core. Detached homes run $550,000 and up. Sandy Springs condos are the exception and are covered as a fallback above.
Alpharetta, Johns Creek, MiltonDetached homes from about $600,000. Milton has no town center.
Chamblee, DoravilleGood location and MARTA, but urban or industrial in character. A DeKalb-Peachtree Airport flight path is nearby.
Smyrna, Peachtree CornersPleasant, but detached homes sit in the $550,000 range and the centers are new-built.
Villa Rica, Douglasville, Dallas, Powder SpringsAffordable with real small-town centers, but 50 to 80 minutes away with thinner hospital access.
Lawrenceville, Snellville, Suwanee, Acworth, CantonEach has a town center worth liking. All run 50 minutes or more at rush hour.
East Point, Stone Mountain, MabletonIn budget, but weak on walkable downtown or commute.
